Hi all, I'm an ML engineer and a math tourist, understanding the Hodge conjecture has been an interest of mine for a long time. I'm working with Claude Fable 5 on implementing pure Hodge structures in Lean 4. As far as my review uncovered, this is the first work of this kind in a proof assistant. https://github.com/thebookersmith/pure-hodge-structures-lean4

What it is:

  • QHodgeStructure record on finite-dimensional ℚ-vector spaces; conjugation σ = conj ⊗ id as a semilinear involution
  • decomposition ↔ opposed-filtration equivalence (Deligne, Hodge II §1.2), both directions, with round trips
  • examples: Tate ℚ(m) and a weight-1 example with the shape of H¹ of an elliptic curve.
  • morphisms and category instance, integral variant
  • On the roadmap: polarizations, tensor/Hom

AI disclosure and breakdown: I work with Claude to author the Lean code, Lean's kernel checks the proofs, I verify with Tier4.lean #print axioms that it rests only on the three axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and with no sorries. I guide Claude on the project itself, planning, and verification, as well as the human presence on zulip.

Citations, credit, and related work:

  • Johan Commelin, Oct 22, 2021, '"there exists a natural Hodge structure on the cohomology of algebraic varieties" is a moral prerequisite to the Hodge conjecture' https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/116395-maths/topic/The.20Hodge.20Conjecture/near/258660974

  • Simone Chiarello, Dec 23, 2025, opened the thread "Complexifications with a view towards Hodge theory", most similar thing I found to my topic: https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Proposal.3A.20Complexifications.20with.20a.20view.20towards.20Hodge.20theory/near/565157710

  • Joël Riou, Dec 27, 2025, Deligne's n-opposed filtrations (Hodge II §1.2) as "the basis for the definition of (pure) Hodge structures" https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Proposal.3A.20Complexifications.20with.20a.20view.20towards.20Hodge.20theory/near/565511365

Mathlib: I am aware of the works and would be excited to find convergence with:

  • #40975: complex structures via a J operator
  • #33954 and forks: filtrations in abstract abelian categories and work on opposed filtrations

Looking forward to discussing and learning in the #maths topic I opened for this! "Pure Hodge structures in Lean 4"

Hi all, I just announced Pure Hodge structures in Lean 4 in #Project announcements, discussing here.
I am interested in your discussion, thoughts, and feedback, for example:

  • Are the definitions faithful to Deligne/Peters–Steenbrink?
  • What's worth upstreaming?
  • Advice on polarization API integration
  • Please build and verify my work as well!
@Booker Smith could you please add a #formalization.yaml file to your repo, if you haven’t done so already?

Should there ultimately be an entry in #AI authored projects for this / should this be there ? Naturally things on this forum are often both “maths/CS” in some sense , even if sometimes applied to natural sciences etc.

But this also seems to be more fitting there perhaps, AI is not currently good at upstreaming however , and likely upstreaming this work, even if it is sound, would be highly nontrivial .

In general I think it’s very very rare for a heavily AI made project to have good upstreaming occur(or any upstreaming at all, a repo that must be human readable and human maintained is often at odds with the incremental goal "grindy" proofs AI come up with , as often their goal is just to fill a term correctly without even needing a math proof to mimic, or consider brittleness to updates at all, it lives frozen in time in its own Lean/mathlib world) .

Hi @Adam Topaz thanks for taking a look so fast. Yes, I just added formalization.yaml to the repo, and CI is green. I also added Challenge.lean, Solution.lean, and comparator.json, with an initial set of the headline claims restated importing only Mathlib, then proven from the project.

@Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 , to address some of your concerns in the discussion here: I agree that upstreaming AI-heavy work should be treated cautiously. On the “grindy” concern, the places I’d point to are OpposedFiltration.toQHodgeStructure in Opposed.lean, the general regrouping lemmas, and the design memos now in design_memos/. We aimed to follow Deligne’s structure and avoid grind-y constructions or term-golf where possible. The plan right now is small, human-defensible pieces per the Mathlib AI policy, with the LLM-generated label, while the library stays a standalone pinned project unless and until particular pieces meet the bar for upstreaming.

Hi all, just an update since the announcement. A fair amount has moved from roadmap to pushed and kernel-checked:

  • Polarizations are up now: Hodge–Riemann orthogonality and positivity, with both example structures (Tate ℚ(m) and the weight-1 elliptic-type example) polarized, sorry-free.
  • Tensor products: weight n ⊗ weight m → weight n+m, with the bigraded pieces as sums over label-splittings.
  • Duals and internal Hom: dual of weight n has weight −n (pieces via dual annihilators); Hom(V,W) = dual(V) ⊗ W.
  • Rigidity layer: Tate twists, evaluation and coevaluation as morphisms of Hodge structures into/out of the weight-0 unit, the double-dual isomorphism, and the zigzag identities at the linear level.
  • Coherence layer: associators, left/right unitors, and the braiding/commutativity isomorphism as morphisms of Hodge structures, with the zigzag identities at the categorical level and the hexagon identity for the underlying maps — together the coherence data of a symmetric rigid tensor structure.
  • Audit is now 126 declarations (40 previously) in Tier4.lean — all still exactly propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound, zero sorries, CI green on every commit.
  • Several general-purpose lemmas came out of this that do not appear to exist in Mathlib: regrouping an internal direct sum along a map on the index type, transport along linear equivalences, and internal-direct-sum projections. These may be upstream candidates.
  • Design memos for each module are public in design_memos/.
